name: the common lab stack
rule: Each domain receives a reproducible, dockerised research environment. NOT every domain gets every component. Keep it minimal and fit for purpose.

layers.name: Applications
layers.holds: domain tools, notebooks, models, UI, dashboards

layers.name: Humanesque components
layers.holds: PANINI, ILM, PEDLER, PRATIK, VIDYA, PAT.AL, AyeAM — as needed, never all

layers.name: GENIE orchestration
layers.holds: composition, tool use, persistent state, cross-domain execution

layers.name: Research software stack
layers.holds: Python, Julia, R, C/C++, MATLAB-compatible workflows, domain libraries, simulation engines

layers.name: Container runtime
layers.holds: Docker or Podman, compose, Kubernetes where the work needs it

layers.name: OS, drivers, firmware
layers.holds: Linux, CUDA/ROCm, hardware interfaces, device permissions

layers.name: Hardware
layers.holds: laptop → workstation → rack → cluster; GPU, CPU, FPGA, MCU, sensors

bench.hardware: laptop plus instruments and an MCU

workstation.reference_unit: ASUS TUF A15, Ryzen 7 7445HS, 16 GB, RTX 3050 4 GB, Radeon 740M — the seed unit named in his corpus

composed.hardware: the union of the labs it crosses

cost_note: Every cost above is 'not established' until a bill of materials is priced with core.bom, where a quote carries its source and its timestamp and an unpriced line blocks the total. 'Low cost' is a measurement, not an adjective.
